title: Ethiopian Roasted Sunflower Seeds
community: Ethiopian markets — the affordable everyday snack
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Roasted Sunflower Seeds — raw sunflower seeds dry-roasted with salt. The most affordable market snack — bought in paper cones from vendors, eaten while shopping or travelling. Ethiopia grows sunflowers widely for oil, and roasted seeds are a natural byproduct.
longDesc: Roasted sunflower seeds are the humble, everyday snack that fills the gap when chickpeas and peanuts are too expensive — always available, always affordable, always satisfying. Sold by street vendors in small paper cones.
ingredients: 2 cups raw sunflower seeds — in shell or shelled
steps: Heat a heavy dry pan over medium heat.
Roast stirring constantly 12—15 minutes until golden and fragrant.
chefTips: Stir constantly — sunflower seeds burn quickly once browning begins.
cookingScience: Sunflower seeds contain high concentrations of vitamin E (tocopherols) — dry roasting actually concentrates these compounds as the moisture evaporates, and some studies suggest roasting may make the vitamin E more bioavailable by breaking down cell walls.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian sunflower — grown for oil production, seeds are a by-product.
culturalNote: Roasted sunflower seeds are the snack of Ethiopia's working poor — affordable, filling, and always available. The vendor with the large tray of roasting seeds, shaking them with a practised circular motion, is a fixture of every Ethiopian market.
